newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Chevron plans $1.2-bln Asian chemical investments.
newsitem.headline: Chevron plans $1.2-bln Asian chemical investments.

text.p: U.S. energy giant Chevron Chemical Co is boosting its Asian profile by embarking on a U.S. $1.2 billion plan to build its first world-scale petrochemical and petroleum additives plants in the region.

"We are in talks to build a large aromatics project in Thailand," Darry Callahan, senior vice president and chief operating officer of Chevron Chemical, said at a news conference to mark the ground breaking of a U.S. $200 million additives, or Oronite, plant in Singapore.
Chevron's lubricating oil and fuel additives plant will be its first world-scale plant in Asia, capable of producing more than 100,000 tonnes per year. Chevron Chemical is part of Chevron Corp.

Callahan said the company was also in talks with the Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) to build a world-scale petrochemical plant, which would use Chevron proprietary technology to produce benzene and paraxylene -- products used to make plastics and textiles.
The total cost of the project would be "in the order of U.S. $1 billion", Callahan said, adding that talks were at an initial stage so he was not able to give a date when construction might start.
A typical world-scale plant produces at least 350,000 tonnes per year of paraxylene and 150,000 tonnes of benzene.

If built, the plant would be Thailand's second aromatics plant. The first, a 650,000-tonnes per year plant run by Aromatics (Thailand) Plc, started production in December and is 44-percent owned by PTT.
Callahan said Chevron was keen to build such a plant in Asia and if talks failed in Thailand the company would seek an alternative host country in the region.
Explaining his choice, Callahan said: "The infrastructure and market for the kind of product we are talking about is growing rapidly in the country (Thailand)."
He said Singapore was the company's second choice.
Chevron's other petrochemical investment plan in the region is an $80 million polystyrene plant in China's eastern Jiangsu province.

The company is building a U.S. $650 million aromatics plant in Saudi Arabia to produce benzene and cyclohexane. The 50-50 joint venture with Saudi Industrial Venture Capital Group will be completed in mid-1999.
Chevron's Oronite additive plant will be located on an island off southern Singapore and will be completed in late 1998.

"We will be spending in total more than U.S. $200 million, which is a very significant investment for the additives industry. Furthermore, the design of this plant is such that we can easily double the capacity when the need arises," Callahan said in a statement.
Chevron said it hopes to raise its share of the U.S.$1 billion Asian additive market to 20-25 percent from the present 15-20 percent, following the start up of the new plant.
The Asian additive market is growing at about eight percent annually, Chevron said.
